1.headline: A Sad Day in a Famous Square
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
A very sad thing happened in a famous square.
It was Saturday afternoon in Krakow, Poland. Many tourists were in the main square. A man drove into the square. He had a big gun. He shot at people.
Six people died. At least fifteen people were hurt. Two police officers were hurt too. The police shot the man. He went to the hospital.
The man is 25 years old. He is from Poland. The police think he was alone. Leaders say he had very extreme ideas.
Things like this do not happen often in Poland. The city will stay open. People will remember the dead until Wednesday.
Again, a man shot many people in Krakow. Six people died.
Thank you for listening.

한 유명한 광장에서 매우 슬픈 일이 일어났습니다.
토요일 오후 폴란드 크라쿠프에서였습니다. 중앙 광장에는 관광객이 많았습니다. 한 남성이 차를 몰고 광장으로 들어왔습니다. 그는 큰 총을 갖고 있었습니다. 그는 사람들에게 총을 쐈습니다.
6명이 숨졌습니다. 최소 15명이 다쳤습니다. 경찰관 2명도 다쳤습니다. 경찰이 그 남성을 쐈습니다. 그는 병원으로 옮겨졌습니다.
남성은 25살입니다. 그는 폴란드 사람입니다. 경찰은 그가 혼자 범행했다고 봅니다. 지도자들은 그가 매우 극단적인 생각을 갖고 있었다고 말합니다.
폴란드에서 이런 일은 자주 일어나지 않습니다. 도시는 계속 문을 열어 둘 것입니다. 사람들은 수요일까지 희생자들을 추모합니다.

2.headline: Gunman Attacks Famous Square in Poland
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
A busy square full of tourists became a place of fear on Saturday.

According to news reports, a man drove into the Main Market Square in Krakow, Poland. He started shooting at people at random. This means he did not choose special people. Six people were killed. At least fifteen people were hurt, and two police officers were among them.

The police shot the man after a gunfight. He was taken to the hospital. He is a 25-year-old Polish man. He wore military-style clothes and a vest that stops bullets. The police believe he acted alone. A government minister said he had very extreme ideas about his nation. Later, three of his family members were found dead in his home in another town.

Shootings like this are very rare in Poland. Krakow is a popular city for tourists. Its old town is famous around the world. The mayor said people will remember the victims until Wednesday. He also said the city will stay open to visitors.
Police are now studying the man's past and his reasons.
To sum up, a gunman killed six people in Krakow's main square. The police think he acted alone.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.
관광객으로 붐비던 광장이 토요일에 공포의 장소가 됐습니다.
보도에 따르면 한 남성이 폴란드 크라쿠프의 중앙 시장 광장으로 차를 몰고 들어왔습니다. 그는 사람들에게 무작위로 총을 쏘기 시작했습니다. 특정한 사람을 고르지 않았다는 뜻입니다. 6명이 숨졌습니다. 최소 15명이 다쳤고, 그중에는 경찰관 2명도 있습니다.

폴란드에서 이런 총격 사건은 매우 드뭅니다. 크라쿠프는 관광객에게 인기 있는 도시입니다. 구시가지는 세계적으로 유명합니다. 시장은 사람들이 수요일까지 희생자들을 추모할 것이라고 말했습니다. 시장은 또 도시가 방문객에게 계속 열려 있을 것이라고 말했습니다.

정리하면, 크라쿠프 중앙 광장에서 한 총격범이 6명을 숨지게 했습니다. 경찰은 그가 단독으로 범행했다고 봅니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

3.headline: Gunman Kills Six in Krakow's Main Square
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
How could a quiet Saturday in one of Europe's most famous squares turn into a tragedy?

According to news reports, a gunman opened fire in Krakow, Poland, on Saturday afternoon. He drove into the city's Main Market Square, a busy area full of tourists, and shot at people at random. Six people were killed, and at least fifteen were hurt. Two police officers were among the injured.

Police said the attacker was a 25-year-old Polish man. He wore military-style clothes and a bulletproof vest, which is a special vest that stops bullets. After a gunfight, police shot him and took him to the hospital. They believe he acted alone. Poland's interior minister said the man held very radical, ultranationalist views. Ultranationalist means having extreme ideas about your own nation. Later, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said three of the man's family members were found dead in his home in another town.

Shootings like this are very rare in Poland. Krakow is one of the country's most visited cities, and its old town is famous around the world. The mayor announced official mourning until Wednesday. Mourning is a time to remember the people who died. He also said the city will stay open to visitors. In Warsaw, the capital, officials added extra security on busy streets.

Why does this matter? Officials are treating the attack very seriously. Poland's defense minister called it an act of terror. Investigators are now looking closely at the man's background and his reasons.
To sum up, a gunman killed six people and hurt at least fifteen in Krakow's main square. Police say he acted alone, and the investigation continues.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.
유럽에서 가장 유명한 광장 가운데 한 곳의 조용한 토요일이 어떻게 비극으로 바뀌었을까요?
보도에 따르면 토요일 오후 폴란드 크라쿠프에서 한 총격범이 총을 쐈습니다. 그는 관광객으로 붐비는 도시의 중앙 시장 광장으로 차를 몰고 들어가 사람들에게 무작위로 총을 쐈습니다. 6명이 숨지고 최소 15명이 다쳤습니다. 다친 사람 중에는 경찰관 2명도 있습니다.

경찰은 범인이 25세 폴란드 남성이라고 밝혔습니다. 그는 군복 같은 옷과 방탄조끼를 입고 있었는데, 방탄조끼는 총알을 막아 주는 특수 조끼입니다. 총격전 끝에 경찰이 그를 쏘아 병원으로 옮겼습니다. 경찰은 그가 단독으로 범행했다고 보고 있습니다. 폴란드 내무장관은 이 남성이 매우 급진적인 극단적 민족주의 견해를 갖고 있었다고 말했습니다. 극단적 민족주의란 자기 나라에 대해 극단적인 생각을 갖는 것을 뜻합니다. 이후 도날드 투스크 총리는 다른 도시에 있는 이 남성의 집에서 가족 3명이 숨진 채 발견됐다고 밝혔습니다.

폴란드에서 이런 총격 사건은 매우 드뭅니다. 크라쿠프는 폴란드에서 관광객이 가장 많이 찾는 도시 가운데 하나이고, 구시가지는 세계적으로 유명합니다. 시장은 수요일까지를 공식 애도 기간으로 선포했습니다. 애도란 세상을 떠난 사람들을 기리는 시간입니다. 시장은 또 도시가 방문객에게 계속 열려 있을 것이라고 말했습니다. 수도 바르샤바에서는 당국이 번화가의 경비를 강화했습니다.
이 일이 왜 중요할까요? 당국은 이번 공격을 매우 심각하게 다루고 있습니다. 폴란드 국방장관은 이를 테러 행위라고 불렀습니다. 수사관들은 지금 이 남성의 배경과 범행 이유를 자세히 살펴보고 있습니다.
정리하면, 크라쿠프 중앙 광장에서 한 총격범이 6명을 숨지게 하고 최소 15명을 다치게 했습니다. 경찰은 그가 단독으로 범행했다고 보고 있으며 수사는 계속되고 있습니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

4.headline: Gunman Kills Six in Krakow's Historic Main Square
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
Poland is in mourning after a rare mass shooting struck the heart of its most popular tourist city.

According to news reports, a gunman drove into the Main Market Square in Krakow's Old Town on Saturday afternoon and fired at people at random. Six people were killed, four women and two men, and at least fifteen others were wounded. Two police officers were among those seriously injured, and five of the injured were foreign nationals.

Police identified the suspect as a 25-year-old Polish citizen. He was wearing military-style fatigues and a bulletproof vest and carried a military-type long gun. Officers shot him during a gunfight near the square, and he was taken to hospital for surgery. Police say he acted alone. At a news conference, Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said the man held very radical, ultranationalist views. Hours later, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the bodies of three of the suspect's close relatives had been found at his home, about 150 kilometers away.

Mass shootings are uncommon in Poland, a country of roughly 37 million people where around 411,000 hold gun permits. Krakow's mayor declared official mourning until Wednesday but stressed that the city would remain open to visitors. In Warsaw, authorities placed road barriers and extra security on major streets in the Old Town.

The attack carries weight beyond Poland's borders. The defense minister described it as an act of terror, and one terrorism expert said the attacker's gear resembled that of other far-right lone attackers in Europe. Investigators are now examining the suspect's background and possible motive.
To sum up, a lone gunman killed six people and wounded at least fifteen in Krakow's Main Market Square, and authorities say he held ultranationalist views. The investigation is ongoing.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스에 오신 것을 환영합니다.
보기 드문 대규모 총격 사건이 최고 인기 관광 도시의 한복판에서 일어나 폴란드가 애도에 잠겼습니다.
보도에 따르면 토요일 오후 한 총격범이 크라쿠프 구시가지의 중앙 시장 광장으로 차를 몰고 들어가 사람들에게 무작위로 총을 쐈습니다. 여성 4명과 남성 2명 등 6명이 숨지고 최소 15명이 다쳤습니다. 중상자 가운데는 경찰관 2명이 있었고, 부상자 중 5명은 외국인이었습니다.

경찰은 용의자가 25세 폴란드 시민이라고 밝혔습니다. 그는 군복 같은 전투복과 방탄조끼를 입고 군용 장총을 들고 있었습니다. 경찰은 광장 근처에서 총격전 중에 그를 쐈고, 그는 수술을 위해 병원으로 옮겨졌습니다. 경찰은 그가 단독으로 범행했다고 말합니다. 마르친 키에르빈스키 내무장관은 기자회견에서 이 남성이 매우 급진적인 극단적 민족주의 견해를 갖고 있었다고 말했습니다. 몇 시간 뒤 도날드 투스크 총리는 약 150킬로미터 떨어진 용의자의 집에서 가까운 친척 3명의 시신이 발견됐다고 밝혔습니다.

이번 공격은 폴란드 국경 너머로도 무게를 갖습니다. 국방장관은 이를 테러 행위라고 표현했으며, 한 테러 전문가는 범인의 장비가 유럽의 다른 극우 단독 공격범들과 비슷했다고 말했습니다. 수사관들은 지금 용의자의 배경과 가능한 동기를 조사하고 있습니다.
정리하면, 단독 총격범이 크라쿠프 중앙 시장 광장에서 6명을 숨지게 하고 최소 15명을 다치게 했으며, 당국은 그가 극단적 민족주의 견해를 갖고 있었다고 밝혔습니다. 수사는 진행 중입니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

5.headline: Lone Gunman Kills Six in Krakow, Shaking a Nation Unused to Mass Shootings
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
A country where mass shootings are almost unheard of is struggling to come to terms with a rampage in the very heart of its best-loved tourist destination.

According to news reports, a gunman drove into the Main Market Square in Krakow's medieval Old Town on Saturday afternoon and opened fire indiscriminately, moving from spot to spot as he shot. Six people were killed, four women and two men, among them a British citizen, while at least fifteen others were wounded, including two police officers who were seriously hurt and five foreign nationals.

Police named the suspect only as a 25-year-old Polish citizen. Clad in military-style fatigues and a bulletproof vest and armed with a military-type long gun, he kept shooting at officers even after being hit, before he was brought down in a gunfight a short distance from the square and taken to hospital for surgery. Investigators believe he acted alone. Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński told reporters that the man held very radical, ultranationalist views and that everything pointed to a fascination with far-right ideology. In a grim twist, Prime Minister Donald Tusk later disclosed that the bodies of three of the suspect's close relatives had been discovered at his home some 150 kilometers to the northeast.

The bloodshed has jolted a nation of roughly 37 million, where about 411,000 people hold gun permits. Krakow's mayor declared a period of official mourning through Wednesday, while insisting that the city would remain open to visitors, and Warsaw's mayor ordered road barriers and beefed-up security across the capital's Old Town.

The implications reach well beyond Poland. The defense minister branded the killings an act of terror, and a terrorism expert observed that the gunman's gear and appearance echoed those of other far-right lone attackers in Europe. Detectives are now piecing together the suspect's background and what drove him to kill.
To sum up, a lone gunman with reported ultranationalist leanings killed six people and wounded at least fifteen in Krakow's historic square, and the investigation into his motive is only beginning.
Thank you for listening.

1.headline: Tesla Will Stop Making a Strange Truck
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Do you know the Cybertruck? It is a very strange car.
The Cybertruck is a truck from Tesla. It is silver and has sharp lines. It looks like a car from a movie.
Now Tesla will stop making it. Elon Musk said this on Friday. The last trucks will come out in 2027.
Why? Not many people bought it. Tesla wants to make a new car. It is a robot taxi. It drives by itself. It has no wheel for a driver.
Did you know? At the first show, the truck's window cracked. People still talk about it.
Again, Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck. It wants to make robot taxis.

3.headline: Tesla Will Stop Making the Cybertruck
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Do you remember the strange, shiny pickup truck that looked like it came from a science fiction movie? Its days are now numbered.

According to news reports, Tesla boss Elon Musk said the company will stop making the Cybertruck. He shared the news in a short post on X on Friday. Production will wind down around the middle of 2027. To wind down means to slowly reduce something until it stops. The truck is built at Tesla's factory near Austin, Texas.
Why is Tesla doing this? Musk said the company wants to make room for more Cybercabs. The Cybercab is a small, two-seat self-driving car. It has no steering wheel and no pedals.

The Cybertruck was first shown in 2019, and sales began in 2023. It is famous for its unusual body made of stainless steel, a strong metal that does not rust. Tesla said it was very tough. But the truck had several recalls. A recall is when a company asks owners to bring a product back to fix a problem. Sales were also lower than hoped. Musk once predicted 250,000 sales a year. In 2025, Tesla sold about 20,000.
Did you know? When the truck was first shown on stage, its "unbreakable" window cracked in front of the crowd.
Why is this interesting? It shows that Tesla is betting its future on cars that drive themselves.
To sum up, Tesla will stop making the Cybertruck by mid-2027 and use the factory space for its Cybercab robotaxi.
Thank you for listening.

4.headline: Tesla to Wind Down Cybertruck Production by Mid-2027
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
The Cybertruck, perhaps the most talked-about vehicle of the decade, is heading for the exit after just a few years on the road.

According to news reports, Tesla chief executive Elon Musk announced in a brief post on X on Friday that Cybertruck production will wind down around the middle of 2027. The stainless-steel pickup is built only at Tesla's gigafactory outside Austin, Texas, and Musk said the change would make room for increased production of the Cybercab, the company's two-seat self-driving vehicle with no steering wheel or pedals. The Cybercab was first shown in 2024 and went into production at the same Texas plant in April.

The Cybertruck was unveiled with great fanfare in 2019 and entered commercial production in 2023 with a starting price of 60,990 dollars. Tesla marketed it as a rugged, almost bulletproof machine that could tow 14,000 pounds. In reality, the truck struggled. It faced numerous recalls, including problems with its rearview camera and pedals. Musk had predicted 250,000 sales a year, but according to Kelley Blue Book figures, Tesla sold just over 20,000 in 2025, roughly half the previous year's total.
Did you know? At the truck's launch event, a demonstration meant to show off its tough armored glass went wrong when a thrown metal ball cracked the window.
Investors appeared to welcome the decision. Tesla's shares rose nearly five percent on Friday. One analyst said the end had been coming for some time, given the high price and weak demand.

Why does it matter? The move signals that Tesla sees its future less in conventional vehicles and more in autonomous robotaxis like the Cybercab, which began carrying passengers in Austin this September.
To sum up, Tesla will phase out the Cybertruck by mid-2027 and shift factory space to its self-driving Cybercab.
Thank you for listening.

5.headline: Tesla Pulls the Plug on the Cybertruck to Bet Big on Robotaxis
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
Few vehicles have divided opinion quite like Tesla's angular, stainless-steel Cybertruck, and now, barely three years after the first deliveries, its time is running out.

According to news reports, Elon Musk revealed in a curt post on X on Friday that production of the pickup will be wound down around the middle of 2027 at Tesla's sprawling plant outside Austin, Texas, the only factory that builds it. The stated rationale is to free up capacity for the Cybercab, a two-seat autonomous vehicle with neither a steering wheel nor pedals, which Tesla unveiled in 2024 and began producing at the same site this spring. Whether the truck might live on at another plant remains unclear, though that appears unlikely.

The Cybertruck made its theatrical debut in 2019 and reached customers in 2023 at a starting price of 60,990 dollars, billed as a near-indestructible rolling fortress capable of towing 14,000 pounds. Reality proved less kind. A string of recalls, involving everything from the rearview camera to the pedals, dented its reputation, and demand never came close to Musk's forecast of 250,000 a year. Kelley Blue Book figures show sales sliding from almost 39,000 in 2024 to around 20,000 last year.
Did you know? At that famous unveiling, a metal ball hurled at the supposedly shatterproof window left it visibly cracked, an awkward moment that instantly went viral.

Wall Street, for its part, seemed relieved: the shares climbed 4.7 percent on Friday, and one prominent analyst remarked that, given the hefty price tag and lackluster demand, the writing had been on the wall for some time.

What makes the decision noteworthy is what it reveals about Tesla's priorities. The company is increasingly staking its future not on eye-catching trucks but on driverless robotaxis such as the Cybercab, which began offering rides in Austin in September. For a brand built on bold, headline-grabbing designs, quietly retiring its most polarizing model marks a telling shift.
To sum up, Tesla is pulling the plug on the Cybertruck by mid-2027, redirecting its Texas factory toward the self-driving Cybercab in a high-stakes bet on autonomy.
Thank you for listening.

1.headline: First Snow in Seoul Comes Early
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
It snowed in Seoul! It was the first snow of the year.
The first snow came on Sunday, November 8. Last year, the first snow came on December 4. So this year, it came 26 days early.
It was not a lot of snow. Only a little snow fell. It did not stay on the ground. But it was cold. In some places, it was below zero.
Be careful on the roads. Some roads can have thin ice. You cannot see it well.
This winter may be warm and wet. There may be more rain and snow.
Again, Seoul had its first snow on Sunday. It came 26 days early.
Thank you for listening.

2.headline: Seoul's First Snow Arrives Early
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Winter came to Seoul much earlier than last year.

According to news reports, Seoul had its first snow on Sunday, November 8. The national weather agency checked it at its weather station in Jongno, in the center of Seoul. Last year, the first snow came on December 4. So this year's snow came 26 days earlier. It was also 12 days earlier than in an average year.

The snow was very light. Only small bits of snow fell for a short time. The snow did not stay on the ground. But the air was cold. In the morning, it was 2.7 degrees in Seoul. Some areas were below zero.
The weather agency told drivers to be careful. In some parts of Gyeonggi and Gangwon, roads may have black ice. This is thin ice that is very hard to see.
What about the rest of winter? The weather agency thinks it will be warmer and wetter than usual. This is because of El Nino, a change in ocean temperatures.
To sum up, Seoul's first snow came 26 days earlier than last year. Stay warm and drive safely.
Thank you for listening.

3.headline: Seoul Sees Its First Snow Almost a Month Early
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Did you see any snowflakes yesterday? If you were in Seoul, winter may have said hello earlier than you expected.

According to news reports, Seoul had its first snow of the season on Sunday, November 8. The Korea Meteorological Administration, the country's weather agency, confirmed it at the official weather station in Jongno District, in central Seoul. This was 26 days earlier than last year, when the first snow came on December 4. It was also 12 days earlier than the average date, which is November 20.

The snow was very light. There were only flurries, which are small amounts of snow that fall for a short time. It did not pile up on the ground in the city. It was also cold. Seoul's morning low on Sunday was 2.7 degrees Celsius, and some parts of the city dropped below zero. Weather officials warned drivers about black ice in parts of Gyeonggi and Gangwon. Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road that is very hard to see.

So, will this winter be very cold? Not necessarily. The weather agency expects a warmer and wetter winter than usual. That is because of El Nino, a natural change in ocean temperatures that can affect weather around the world. It may bring more rain and snow this season.
To sum up, Seoul's first snow arrived 26 days earlier than last year. Drive carefully, and keep a warm coat close by.
Thank you for listening.

4.headline: Seoul Records First Snowfall 26 Days Earlier Than Last Year
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
Winter has arrived in the capital ahead of schedule, nearly a month earlier than it did a year ago.

According to news reports, the Korea Meteorological Administration confirmed that Seoul saw its first snowfall of the season on Sunday, November 8. The snow was recorded at the official Seoul weather station in Jongno District. That is 26 days earlier than last year's first snow on December 4, and 12 days ahead of the 30-year average of November 20. Local media noted that it was the earliest first snow in the capital since 2010.

The snowfall itself was modest. Only light flurries fell, and weather officials said the amount was too small to accumulate in the city. Temperatures, however, dropped sharply. Seoul's morning low on Sunday was 2.7 degrees Celsius, while parts of the city, including Nowon and Eunpyeong, dipped below freezing. In Daegwallyeong, in Gangwon Province, the mercury fell to minus 5.4 degrees. The agency warned that rain or snow could freeze into black ice on roads in northeastern Gyeonggi and inland areas of Gangwon. It added that snow could pile up on mountains around 1,000 meters high in northeastern Gyeonggi.

Despite the early chill, forecasters do not expect a harsh winter overall. The weather agency predicts a warmer and wetter season than usual as El Nino strengthens. Warm, moist winds from the south could push temperatures above normal and bring more frequent rain and snow.
For commuters, the practical advice is simple: watch for slippery roads in the coming days, especially on Tuesday, when morning temperatures in Seoul are forecast to hover around zero.
To sum up, Seoul's first snow came 26 days earlier than last year, but the overall winter is expected to be milder and wetter than usual.
Thank you for listening.

5.headline: Seoul's First Snow Lands Nearly a Month Early as Cold Snap Bites
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
If Sunday's sudden chill caught you off guard, you were not alone: winter has turned up in Seoul almost four weeks ahead of last year's timetable.

According to news reports, the Korea Meteorological Administration confirmed that the capital logged its first snowfall of the season on Sunday, November 8, as observed at the official Seoul weather station in Jongno District. That puts it a full 26 days ahead of last year, when the first flakes did not appear until December 4, and 12 days earlier than the 1991 to 2020 average of November 20. Domestic media reported that it was Seoul's earliest first snow since 2010, although the record still belongs to October 23, 1981.

In truth, the snowfall was more symbolic than substantial. A smattering of light flurries drifted down, but officials said the precipitation was far too meager to settle on city streets. The cold, by contrast, was very real. Seoul's morning low stood at 2.7 degrees Celsius, with outlying districts such as Nowon and Eunpyeong slipping below freezing, while the mountain pass of Daegwallyeong in Gangwon Province shivered at minus 5.4 degrees. Forecasters cautioned that lingering moisture could glaze roads with treacherous black ice in northeastern Gyeonggi and inland Gangwon. Higher ground told a different story, however, with the agency saying snow could build up on peaks of around 1,000 meters in northeastern Gyeonggi.

Paradoxically, this early taste of winter is not a harbinger of a brutal season. The weather agency anticipates a milder and wetter winter than usual, as a strengthening El Nino steers warm, moisture-laden air northward, potentially nudging temperatures above the norm and making rain and snow more frequent. November itself is also expected to be wetter than usual.
For now, the takeaway for commuters is to tread carefully, particularly on Tuesday, when the mercury in Seoul is expected to hover around zero at dawn.
To sum up, Seoul's first snow arrived 26 days earlier than a year ago, yet forecasters expect the winter as a whole to be milder and wetter than normal.
Thank you for listening.
